prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance forward, lifts uke up so that the right elbow enters under uke's left armpit, overlaps with uke, and: using the extension of both knees, the hikite (pulling hand) and the lifted right arm: loads uke onto the hips and throws uke forward.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall) From kumi-kata, tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki, loads uke onto the hips and throws forward; uke lands taking ukemi. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) to break uke's balance forward, and throws uke forward. How to take the ukemi: In time with tori's tsurikomi-goshi, uke does not pull the hips back and takes mae-mawari-ukemi (forward rolling breakfall). Cooperation of uke: So that tori does not bend forward, uke arches the upper body moderately even when lifted.

Tori throws uke forward without lifting uke off the mat. Tori uses mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement) and throws uke forward without lifting uke up. How to take the ukemi: Uke rotates sideways about the right foot and takes yoko-ukemi (side breakfall).

Tori pushes uke; at the moment uke stops, tori turns in with mae-mawari-sabaki and applies the technique. Push uke, and at the moment uke comes to a stop, apply the technique with mae-mawari-sabaki (forward turning body movement).

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Do not apply the technique with tori's elbow sticking out to the side. Uke's balance is not broken sufficiently, and tori's own balance collapses backwards.
Do not apply the technique bent forward, in a posture that drives the head into the mat.
